General information.Name: Environmental impact of beef production in Mexico through life cycle assessment
General information.Category: Agriculture, Forestry, Fishing and Hunting/112 Animal Production and Aquaculture
General information.Description: Intensive and extensive systems of beef production in the Mexican tropics were analyzed. The aim of the study was to estimate and compare the environmental impact of two typical beef production systems in Veracruz, Mexico. A system boundary was established from farm production to prior to transport for consumer consumption, including intermediate stages of product processing, marketing and transportation. The functional unit was 1 kg of boneless and fatless beef. The life cycle inventory was built using information from case studies; farmers, slaughterhouses and retail point managers who provided information from records and expert knowledge were interviewed. The study included cow-calf processes, pre-fattening, fattening, processing and retail. Several impact categories were analyzed using SimaPro software and the ReCiPe Midpoint method for impact characterization. The results showed that for the extensive system, the cow-calf stage is the major contributor in eleven of the twelve impact categories analyzed, while in the intensive system, it is the main contributor to the climate change, terrestrial acidification, freshwater and marine eutrophication. The fattening stage of intensive system, has a predominant impact on human toxicity, water depletion, terrestrial ecotoxicity, fossil depletion, photo-oxidants formation, freshwater ecotoxicity and marine ecotoxicity; the processing stage has relevant contributions to fossil fuel depletion and the formation of photochemical oxidants in intensive systems. Finally, the marketing stage did not have a predominant impact on any category. The results indicated that the extensive system has better environmental performance than the intensive system for nine of the twelve studied categories. According last, it is important to improve the reproductive performance in calf breeding herds to mitigate emissions in the beef production chain as well as to improve livestock food quality in the extensive system for the mitigation of GHG emissions due to enteric fermentation.
General information.Tags: Life cycle assessment of Mexican beef, Extensive and intensive beef production, Mexican beef supply chain, Environmental impact assessment of beef production, Beef production in the Mexican tropic
General information.Technology Description: The analysis was performed using SimaPro 7.3.3 (PRé Consultants, 2014) software for processing the inventory. The impact assessment method used was ReCiPe Midpoint (H) method version 1.06. Methane, nitrous oxide and ammonia emissions were estimated using the Tier 1 methodology of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) Volume 4 (IPCC, 2006), based on livestock population data and default emission factors.

processDocumentation.LCI method: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) based on ISO 14040/14044 standards. The impact assessment was conducted using the ReCiPe Midpoint (H) method version 1.06.
processDocumentation.Process type: Cradle-to-retail gate process for beef production.
processDocumentation.Modeling constants: The system boundary was from farm production to prior to transport for consumer consumption, including cow-calf, pre-fattening, fattening, processing and marketing. Infrastructure and equipment were not considered. For the cow-calf stage (a combined milk and calf system), an economic allocation was used, assigning 35.5% of the environmental impact to calf production. The electricity mix corresponded to the average for Mexico during 2008 (22% hydro, 22% natural gas, 5% coal, 3% nuclear, 0.2% wind and 48% combined cycle).
processDocumentation.Data source information: The life cycle inventory was built using primary data from 17 case studies in Veracruz, Mexico, through interviews with farmers, slaughterhouse representatives, and marketing point sellers. This was supplemented by values from the literature, expert interviews, and domestic statistics. Key sources include FIRA (2015), IPCC (2006), SENER (2010), and others listed in the references.
processDocumentation.Data completeness: The study covers the main stages of the beef production chain: cow-calf, pre-fattening, fattening, processing, and retail. It includes inputs like animal feed, fertilizers, water, energy, packaging, and transportation, as well as outputs like emissions and waste. Infrastructure and equipment are excluded.
processDocumentation.Data selection: The study focuses on two representative systems in Veracruz, Mexico: Intensive (IS) and Extensive (ES). This JSON focuses on the Intensive System. Infrastructure and equipment were excluded from the system boundary.
processDocumentation.Data treatment: Emissions from enteric fermentation and manure were estimated using the Tier 1 methodology of the IPCC (2006). Data from case studies, literature, and official statistics were consolidated and validated with experts to build the LCI.
processDocumentation.Sampling procedure: Information was gathered from 17 case studies, which included interviews with 2 ranches for cow-calf, 2 case studies per process (pre-fattening, fattening, processing) for each system, 1 convenience store for marketing, and 2 butcher houses for the extensive system.
processDocumentation.Data collection period: The paper was published in 2016, with some data, like the electricity mix, from 2008. The specific period for field data collection is not explicitly stated.
processDocumentation.Use advice: The results are specific to the typical beef production systems in the Mexican tropics (Veracruz) and may not be representative of other regions or production systems. The exclusion of infrastructure and equipment should be considered when comparing results.
processDocumentation.Completeness: The study is considered comprehensive within its defined cradle-to-retail-gate boundaries, including several life cycle stages. However, the aggregated LCI data per functional unit is not provided in the publication.
